action: GMO Pepabo advises resetting passwords through the official user page rather than email links, reviewing Basic authentication settings, and staying alert to phishing because it will not ask for passwords or card details by email or phone.
date_note: The page gives 27 November as the disclosure day; the company detected the suspicious downloads on 24 November.

evidence.quote: 現時点の対象件数は51万6,564件です。

exec: GMO Pepabo says 516,564 Lolipop! customer records are affected so far and that the count may still change.
geo_basis: country (company location not stated in the source)
plain: GMO Pepabo says customer data from its Lolipop! hosting services was taken after unauthorized access to its internal systems. It says 516,564 records are affected so far, and the count may change.

sources.name: Rocket Boys Security Measures Lab, 27 Nov 2026 (relays GMO Pepabo's notice and Q&A)

summary: According to Rocket Boys, GMO Pepabo said it detected suspicious data downloads on 24 November while checking audit logs of its data analytics platform, after unauthorized access to internal systems. The company says the number affected is 516,564 for now. Names, email addresses and some initial passwords are included; the company says credit card and bank account data were not affected.
title: GMO Pepabo says Lolipop! customer data was taken after unauthorized access to internal systems; 516,564 records affected so far

validation.note: Only Rocket Boys (27 Nov), which quotes GMO Pepabo's notice and Q&A, was read; GMO Pepabo's own page was not found or read.

review.note: stronger than source: access was to internal systems, not stated as analytics platform; title and plain fixed
